evidence: src/services/data-provider/interfaces/data-provider.interface.ts: DataProviderInterface (canHandle, getAssetProfile, getDividends, getHistorical, getQuotes, search, getName, getTestSymbol) plus its parameter types GetAssetProfileParams, GetDividendsParams, GetHistoricalParams, GetQuotesParams and GetSearchParams. All of these describe the provider contract.

src/services/data-provider/interfaces/data-enhancer.interface.ts: DataEnhancerInterface.enhance({requestTimeout, response, symbol}) returns Promise<Partial<SymbolProfile>>. Its getName and getTestSymbol follow the same pattern as the provider interface.
Both files work on Prisma SymbolProfile and accept requestTimeout and symbol in the same way, so they share one abstraction vocabulary.
Minor: GetDividendsParams and GetHistoricalParams are structurally identical (from, granularity?, requestTimeout?, symbol, to). This repeats a shape, not a rule or invariant.
Minor: DataEnhancerInterface.enhance declares its parameter object inline, while every DataProviderInterface method uses a named *Params interface.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has two contract files for the data-provider subsystem. data-provider.interface.ts defines what a market-data source must provide, and data-enhancer.interface.ts defines the step that post-processes a SymbolProfile. Both are pure type contracts in the same domain and are used together by DataProviderService, the provider implementations and the enhancer services. Neither file contains logic, so no rule or invariant is repeated, and nothing bypasses the module's abstractions. There are two small style issues: GetDividendsParams and GetHistoricalParams have identical shapes, and DataEnhancerInterface.enhance declares its parameter type inline instead of as a named *Params interface like the provider methods do. These are inconsistencies in how request shapes are declared. They don't split the module's concern or duplicate a rule, so they don't meet the fail criteria.
